analysis.title: What's Top of Mind in Macro Research: Oil flow normalization, lower US inflation, later Fed hike
key_insights: Goldman estimates Persian Gulf oil exports have recovered to their 2025 average, driven by higher Saudi crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz, while the Middle East conflict continues.
Recovered Gulf exports plus continued weakness in China's crude imports over several months support the base case for Brent at $85/bbl by year-end 2026 and $80/bbl in 2027.

Diesel supplies have been much less resilient than crude supplies. US policymakers are considering diesel export restrictions, which GS estimates would push US diesel prices moderately lower near term but could raise ex-US diesel prices and eventually US retail gasoline prices.
After the softer-than-expected August core PCE report, GS now expects core PCE of 3.0% in 2026 (Q4/Q4), below the median FOMC participant forecast of 3.4%.

Based on the core PCE miss and recent comments from NY Fed President John Williams, GS pushed its expected next Fed hike to December from October. GS sees a strong chance the Fed concludes further hikes are unnecessary, with the US labor market expected to stay relatively stable.

Easing inflation and limited Fed tightening support GS's broadly benign macro outlook. Higher yields and energy prices are the main risks to the constructive market view, but both markets already embed significant risk premiums, so GS sees more paths to relief.

GS lowered its 3/6/12-month USD/JPY forecasts to 158/155/150 from 162/163/165, citing Japanese monetary policy developments and possible Japanese investor reallocation toward domestic assets, which make long JPY more attractive and valuation a bigger driver.
GS expects AI hyperscaler capex to rise substantially in 2027 and exceed the $1.2tn consensus, though growth and upside surprises should diminish relative to recent quarters.

GS equity analysts estimate hyperscalers need about $300bn of annual AI revenue in the next few years to break even on capex, and about $450bn+ for a 15% ROIC. Estimated AI revenues are below that threshold but growing quickly with sizable backlogs.

Prediction markets imply over 60% odds of a Democratic Senate majority and over 90% odds of a Democratic House majority in the US midterms. US equities could show higher volatility into the elections and a rally after, though a Democratic sweep with a tougher AI legislative agenda could reverse that pattern.

Brazil's general election this weekend is polling toward a second-round runoff between Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro. GS thinks a fiscally unfriendly outcome would weigh on Brazilian assets, with downside smaller than the potential rally in local rates from a market-friendly result.
